parts.label: Part 1
parts.title: Learning by Examples
parts.article:
Learning by Examples
 
(A) Learning Theory is rooted in the work of Ivan Pavlov, the famous scientist who discovered and documented the principles governing how animals (humans included) learn in the 1900s. Two basic kinds of learning or conditioning occur, one of which is famously known as the classical conditioning. Classical conditioning happens when an animal learns to associate a neutral stimulus (signal) with a stimulus that has intrinsic meaning based on how closely in time the two stimuli are presented. The classic example of classical conditioning is a dog's ability to associate the sound of a bell (something that originally has no meaning to the dog) with the presentation of food (something that has a lot of meaning to the dog) a few moments later. Dogs are able to learn the association between bell and food, and will salivate immediately after hearing the bell once this connection has been made. Years of learning research have led to the creation of a highly precise learning theory that can be used to understand and predict how and under what circumstances most any animal will learn, including human beings, and eventually help people figure out how to change their behaviours.
 
(B) Role models are a popular notion for guiding child development, but in recent years very interesting research has been done on learning by examples in other animals. If the subject of animal learning is taught very much in terms of classical or operant conditioning, it places too much emphasis on how we allow animals to learn and not enough on how they are equipped to learn. To teach a course of mine, I have been dipping profitably into a very interesting and accessible compilation of papers on social learning in mammals, including chimps and human children, edited by Heyes and Galef (1996).
 
(C) The research reported in one paper started with a school field trip to Israel to a pine forest where many pine cones were discovered, stripped to the central core. So the investigation started with no weighty theoretical intent, but was directed at finding out what was eating the nutritious pine seeds and how they managed to get them out of the cones. The culprit proved to be the versatile and athletic black rat (Rattus rattus), and the technique was to bite each cone scale off at its base, in sequence from base to top following the spiral growth pattern of the cone.
 
(D) Urban black rats were found to lack the skill and were unable to learn it even if housed with experienced cone strippers. However, infants of urban mothers cross-fostered by stripper mothers acquired the skill, whereas infants of stripper mothers fostered by an urban mother could not. Clearly the skill had to be learned from the mother. Further elegant experiments showed that naive adults could develop the skill if they were provided with cones from which the first complete spiral of scales had been removed; rather like our new photocopier which you can work out how to use once someone has shown you how to switch it on. In the case of rats, the youngsters take cones away from the mother when she is still feeding on them, allowing them to acquire the complete stripping skill.
 
(E) A good example of adaptive bearing we might conclude, but let’s see the economies. This was determined by measuring oxygen uptake of a rat stripping a cone in a metabolic chamber to calculate energetic cost and comparing it with the benefit of the pine seeds measured by calorimeter. The cost proved to be less than 10% of the energetic value of the cone. An acceptable profit margin.
 
(F) A paper in 1996, Animal Behaviour by Bednekoff and Baida, provides a different view of the adaptiveness of social learning. It concerns the seed caching behaviour of Clark's Nutcracker (Nucifraga columbiana) and the Mexican Jay (Aphelocoma ultramarina). The former is a specialist, caching 30,000 or so seeds in scattered locations that it will recover over the months of winter; the Mexican Jay will also cache food but is much less dependent upon this than the Nutcracker. The two species also differ in their social structure: the Nutcracker being rather solitary while the Jay forages in social groups.
 
(G) The experiment is to discover not just whether a bird can remember where it hid a seed but also if it can remember where it saw another bird hide a seed. The design is slightly comical with a cacher bird wandering about a room with lots of holes in the floor hiding food in some of the holes, while watched by an observer bird perched in a cage. Two days later, cachers and observers are tested for their discovery rate against an estimated random performance. In the role of cacher, not only the Nutcracker but also the less specialised Jay performed above chance; more surprisingly, however, jay observers were as successful as jay cachers whereas nutcracker observers did no better than chance. It seems that, whereas the Nutcracker is highly adapted at remembering where it hid its own seeds, the social living Mexican Jay is more adept at remembering, and so exploiting, the caches of others.

questions.question: A comparison between rats’ learning and human learning

analyses.content: 不要选A，A段虽然提到了人类学习，但那是在讲普遍理论，真正的“对比（comparison）”出现在D段复印机的类比中。

(D段) Further elegant experiments showed that naive adults could develop the skill if they were provided with cones from which the first complete spiral of scales had been removed; rather like our new photocopier which you can work out how to use once someone has shown you how to switch it on.
D段将老鼠通过观察母亲学习剥松果的技能，比作人类观察别人开机后就能学会使用复印机。

questions.question: A reference to the earliest study in animal learning

analyses.content: A段开头提到了巴甫洛夫（Ivan Pavlov）在1900年代的工作，这是动物学习研究的根源和最早记录。
看到“rooted in”和“1900s”就要意识到这在指向“earliest study（最早的研究）”。
(A段) Learning Theory is rooted in the work of Ivan Pavlov, the famous scientist who discovered and documented the principles governing how animals (humans included) learn in the 1900s.

questions.question: The discovery of who stripped the pine cone

analyses.content: C段描述了研究者通过调查发现，剥开松果的“罪魁祸首（culprit）”原来是黑鼠。
这一段描述了寻找凶手的整个调查过程，符合“discovery”的信息点。

(C段) So the investigation started with no weighty theoretical intent, but was directed at finding out what was eating the nutritious pine seeds and how they managed to get them out of the cones. The culprit proved to be the versatile and athletic black rat (Rattus rattus)...

questions.question: A description of a cost-effectiveness experiment

analyses.content: 文中提到的“acceptable profit margin（可接受的利润率）”就是“cost-effectiveness（成本效益）”的直白表达。
E段通过测量氧气消耗（成本）和松子热量（收益）来计算老鼠剥松果是否划算。

(E段) This was determined by measuring oxygen uptake of a rat stripping a cone in a metabolic chamber to calculate energetic cost and comparing it with the benefit of the pine seeds measured by calorimeter. The cost proved to be less than 10% of the energetic value of the cone.

groups.description:
Reading Passage 1 has seven paragraphs A-G.
Which paragraph contains the following information?
Write the correct letter A-G in boxes 1-4 on your answer sheet.

questions.question: The field trip to Israel was to investigate how black rats learn to strip pine cones.

analyses.content: 原文说这次实地考察起初并没有沉重的理论意图，只是偶然发现了剥开的松果才开始调查，并非一开始就为了研究黑鼠。
题目说“为了调查黑鼠如何学习”，而原文说“started with no weighty theoretical intent（开始时没有理论目的）”。

(C段) The research reported in one paper started with a school field trip to Israel to a pine forest where many pine cones were discovered, stripped to the central core. So the investigation started with no weighty theoretical intent, but was directed at finding out what was eating the nutritious pine seeds...

questions.question: The pine cones were stripped from bottom to top by black rats.

analyses.content: 原文明确提到黑鼠剥松果的顺序是“从底部到顶部（from base to top）”。
题目中的“bottom”对应文中的“base”，方向完全吻合。

(C段) The culprit proved to be the versatile and athletic black rat (Rattus rattus), and the technique was to bite each cone scale off at its base, in sequence from base to top following the spiral growth pattern of the cone.

questions.question: It can be learned from other relevant experiences to use a photocopier.

analyses.content: (D段) Further elegant experiments showed that naive adults could develop the skill... rather like our new photocopier which you can work out how to use once someone has shown you how to switch it on.
这里的“shown you how to switch it on”就是题目里“other relevant experiences（其他相关经验）”的体现。
D段提到，一旦有人展示了如何开关（相关经验），你就能摸索出如何使用复印机。

questions.question: Stripping the pine cones is an instinct of the black rats.

analyses.content: 实验证明，如果幼鼠不跟着剥松果的母亲学习，它们就掌握不了这项技能，说明这是后天学习而非本能。
题目说是“instinct（本能）”，原文强调“Clearly the skill had to be learned（显然必须通过学习获得）”，两者相反。

(D段) Clearly the skill had to be learned from the mother. Further elegant experiments showed that naive adults could develop the skill if they were provided with cones from which the first complete spiral of scales had been removed...

groups.contentHtml: While the Nutcracker is more able to cache seeds, the Jay relies on caching food and is thus less specialised in this ability, but more . To study their behaviour of caching and finding their caches, an experiment was designed and carried out to test these two birds for their ability to remember where they hid the seeds. In the experiment, the cacher bird hid seeds in the ground while the other . As a result, the Nutcracker and the Mexican Jay showed different performance in the role of at finding the seeds- the observing didn’t do as well as its counterpart.

analyses.content: 原文提到墨西哥松鸦虽然也储藏食物，但对这一行为的依赖程度远低于（much less dependent）星鸦。
根据对比关系，星鸦是专家，松鸦则是“much less dependent”。
(F段) The former [Nutcracker] is a specialist, caching 30,000 or so seeds... the Mexican Jay will also cache food but is much less dependent upon this than the Nutcracker.
(F段) The two species also differ in their social structure: the Nutcracker being rather solitary while the Jay forages in social groups.
原文指出这两种鸟的社会结构不同，松鸦是在“社会群体（social groups）”中觅食的。
此处形容松鸦的特性，对应文中的“forages in social groups”。
实验设计中，一只鸟在地上埋种子，另一只作为观察者的鸟在笼子里“观看（watched）”。
空格处需要一个动词描述观察者的动作，文中直接给出了“watched”。
(G段) The design is slightly comical with a cacher bird wandering about a room... while watched by an observer bird perched in a cage.
实验结果显示，星鸦和松鸦在扮演“观察者（observer）”角色寻找种子时表现出了差异。
后面半句提到了“observing”，暗示这里讨论的是作为观察者的表现。
(G段) In the role of cacher, not only the Nutcracker but also the less specialised Jay performed above chance; more surprisingly, however, jay observers were as successful as jay cachers...
实验发现，星鸦观察者寻找种子的成功率并不比随机乱找高，表现不如松鸦观察者。
根据文中“nutcracker observers did no better than chance”，说明表现不好的观察者是星鸦。
(G段) ...whereas nutcracker observers did no better than chance. It seems that... the social living Mexican Jay is more adept at remembering...
